title: Field Performance of TiO2–Epoxy Coatings on Concrete Panels: Effects of Nanoparticle Loading, Exposure Location, and Weathering Duration on  CO Concentrations
content: This study examined carbon monoxide (CO) concentrations associated with titanium dioxide (TiO₂)-modified epoxy coatings applied to concrete panels exposed at three roadside locations in coastal Peru. The experimental study followed a balanced 4 × 3 × 3 factorial arrangement with four nominal TiO₂ contents (0%, 3%, 5%, and 7%), three locations (Chilca, San Bartolo, and Lurín), and three outdoor-exposure periods (7, 14, and 28 days), comprising 108 panels as described in the experimental record. Gas con-centrations were recorded using temporary enclosures placed over the panels, rather than continuous open-air monitoring. Mean CO readings declined from 1.0918 ppm for the epoxy-only control to 0.5986 ppm at 7% TiO₂, corresponding to an absolute dif-ference of 0.4932 ppm (45.17% relative to the control). The factorial analysis yielded a main effect of TiO₂ content (F = 397.7548, p < 0.001), whereas the main effect on CO₂ was not statistically significant (p = 0.07431). Historical Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI CO columns (2021–2025) exhibited the same rank ordering across locations as the experi-mental controls, although the satellite and panel observations were not temporally matched. The results document an association between TiO₂ formulation and enclosed CO readings; they do not independently establish photocatalytic oxidation, field-scale air purification, or satellite validation. The absence of documented sensor calibration, chamber blank tests, and full measurement-level traceability is considered when in-terpreting these findings.
